data.title: Position
data.tagline: Place an element in normal flow, against a parent, or against the viewport
data.description: CSS position decides how an element is placed and whether offsets such as top and left apply. Relative often creates a reference for an absolutely positioned child; fixed follows the viewport; sticky moves only within its scrolling context. Choose the mode from the relationship you need.

use: Anchor a badge to an icon
Fix a floating control to the viewport
Create a reference for an overlay inside a component
Keep normal content in document flow by default
avoid: Absolutely position the main page layout
Use fixed coordinates that only fit one screen
Remove content from flow without reserving its space
Choose a position mode before identifying its reference box

lessonPractice.title: A New badge must stay on the top-right of its product card and move and wrap with the card. What positioning is most reliable?

options.label: Establish the card as the positioning reference and absolutely position the badge at its top-right
options.feedback: Once the parent card is the reference, badge offsets are calculated from it and move with the whole card.

options.label: Fix the badge to the viewport's top-right and tune offsets to match the card
options.feedback: Fixed positioning follows the viewport rather than the card, so scrolling and wrapping separate badge from target.

options.label: Only set absolute with large top and right values and leave every parent unchanged
options.feedback: Without the intended reference, the badge may position against a distant containing block and drift as layout changes.

data.agentPrompt: Make each product card the positioning reference and place its badge absolutely at the card's top-right, without viewport-based fixed coordinates. Test varied card heights, grid column changes, and page scrolling.
